chief_complaint.reason: Reported more secretions and suctioning needs in his son with a tracheostomy.
chief_complaint.speaker: Caller
chief_complaint.quote: It's his trach. He has a lot more secretions. For the last two days.
chief_complaint.explanation: Documents the problem prompting the call.

assessment.text: Suctioning was needed about every two hours for the last two days.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: I'm suctioning him about every two hours now. Before, it was every four.

assessment.text: Clear thin secretions were reported.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Clear. Thin and clear. Not yellow, not green.

assessment.text: Temperature was 98.6.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: No. I took it a few minutes ago. Ninety eight point six.

assessment.text: Breathing was easy and his color was good.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: No, no. His breathing is easy. His color is good.

assessment.text: He had a mild cough when secretions built up.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: A little. A mild cough. Just when the secretions build up.

assessment.text: He had the sniffles on Sunday.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: He did have the sniffles on Sunday. Maybe that's it.

assessment.text: He had about six suction catheters left.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: I have about six left. At this rate, that's just a couple of days.

assessment.text: Oxygen saturation read 97 or 98 every night.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: It reads ninety seven, ninety eight. No alarms in the last few days, thankfully.

response.text: Planned a respiratory therapist visit tomorrow.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'd like our respiratory therapist to see him tomorrow, just to check everything.

response.text: Planned to order ten French suction catheters.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll put in an order for ten French catheters. They should come tomorrow.

response.text: Planned to order the catheters.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll order those now. What size does he use?

education.text: Advised suctioning as needed and writing down the color and amount.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: Perfect. Suction him as needed, whenever he sounds wet or coughs. And write down the color and amount, so we can see if it changes.

education.text: Advised a fresh catheter each time and calling if he ran short.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: In the meantime, use a fresh catheter each time, as usual. If you run short before they come, call me and I'll see about getting a few from the on-call stock.

education.text: Advised calling for yellow, green, bloody secretions, fever, or harder breathing, and calling 911 for blue color or a blocked tube.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: If his secretions turn yellow or green, or have blood, or he gets a fever, or he's working harder to breathe, call us. And if he turns blue, or the tube is blocked and you can't clear it, call nine one one.

chief_complaint.reason: Gave an update on her husband's condition near the end of life.
chief_complaint.speaker: Caller
chief_complaint.quote: I'm calling about my husband, Walter.
chief_complaint.explanation: Documents the reason for the call.

assessment.text: He had been sleeping about twenty hours a day for about five days.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: He's sleeping a lot. A whole lot. About twenty hours a day, I'd say, now. For about five days.

assessment.text: He was eating and drinking very little, with a few sips of water and two spoonfuls of ice cream today.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Hardly anything. A few sips of water. And two spoonfuls of ice cream today. That's all.

assessment.text: He had no pain and looked peaceful.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: I don't think so. He's not grimacing, he's not moaning. He looks peaceful.

assessment.text: He had occasional pauses in his breathing, stopping for a few seconds and then taking a big breath.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Sometimes there are pauses. He'll stop for a few seconds, and then take a big breath. It scares the kids.

assessment.text: He was passing urine less, once or twice a day, dark yellow.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Less. The brief is only wet once or twice a day now. It's dark yellow.

assessment.text: Lorazepam 0.5 mg was given once two nights ago for restlessness and he settled.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Once. Two nights ago. He was restless, and he was picking at his sheet. I gave him one. He settled right down and slept.

assessment.text: Metoprolol, atorvastatin and tamsulosin were stopped last week because he could no longer swallow them.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: We stopped those last week. The doctor said we could, since he couldn't swallow them anymore.

response.text: Advised giving lorazepam as needed for restlessness, even in the middle of the night.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: Yes. Even in the middle of the night. You don't need to call first.

response.text: Planned a nurse visit tomorrow morning.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll arrange a visit tomorrow morning.

response.text: Planned to message the chaplain tonight to ask her to call.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll message our chaplain tonight, and ask her to call you.

education.text: Advised not forcing food or fluids and keeping his mouth moist with a swab and lip balm.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: please don't force food or fluids.

education.text: Advised turning him gently every two hours and playing his favorite music.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: turn him gently every two hours, so he's comfortable.

education.text: Advised calling at any time, day or night.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: you can call us any time, day or night.

education.text: Advised calling first before calling 911 or the funeral home, and that the nurse would come and help with everything.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: Call us first. Please don't call 911 or the funeral home before you call us.

chief_complaint.reason: Reported drainage and pain at a toe amputation site.
chief_complaint.speaker: Caller
chief_complaint.quote: I think there's something going on with it.
chief_complaint.explanation: Documents the problem prompting the call.

assessment.text: The toe was draining pale yellow fluid and smelled slightly, with the dressing wet through by lunch.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: It started yesterday. It was dry before. Today the dressing was wet through, yellowish.

assessment.text: The toe pain was a throbbing ache of 4/10, worse yesterday.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: A four. A four out of ten. It aches. It's a throbbing ache.

assessment.text: Temperature was 99.6.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Ninety nine point six. So a little warm.

assessment.text: Cephalexin 500 mg four times a day was taken, day 5 of 10, last dose at noon.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: The cephalexin. Five hundred milligrams. Four times a day. I'm on day five of ten. I took one at noon.

assessment.text: The dressing was changed once a day, washed hands, and the foot was raised.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: Once a day. I wash my hands. I take the old one off, I look at it, I put a new one on.

assessment.text: No chills were reported.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: No chills. I felt kind of warm last night. No shaking.

assessment.text: No red streaks were reported.
assessment.speaker: Caller
assessment.quote: I looked. I used the mirror. It's red around the edge of the dressing, but no streaks. Nothing climbing up. Just the, around the wound.

response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'm going to send a message to the wound clinician about the drainage and the smell, so they can decide if they want to change anything.
response.explanation: Documents the planned message to the team.

response.text: Planned a nurse visit for tomorrow.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'm scheduling a nurse visit for tomorrow, so she can look at it in person.

response.text: Planned to order more dressing supplies.
response.speaker: Nurse
response.quote: I'll order more. I'll send plenty.

education.text: Advised changing the dressing once a day or when soaked, washing hands, keeping the foot raised, and keeping the dressing dry.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: Once a day, or when it's soaked. Wash hands. Keep your foot raised on a pillow when you're sitting. And keep the dressing dry.

education.text: Advised finishing every dose of the antibiotic, spaced evenly and with food.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: finish every dose of the antibiotic. Even if the toe looks better. Take it evenly spaced and with food.

education.text: Advised calling right away for a temperature of 101 or higher, chills, red streaks, heavy drainage, or worse pain.
education.speaker: Nurse
education.quote: If your temperature goes to one hundred one or higher, if you get chills, if you see red streaks going up the foot, if the drainage gets heavy, or the pain gets worse, call us right away.
